thread_text:
alex: quick heads-up — seeing low-rate single-bit ECC increments across 3 racks in us-west-2. not XID, no driver churn. could be a bitrot-like pattern. raising here to sync.

meera: ack. when did this start?

alex: around 03:12 UTC, count ramped from baseline ~0.1/min to 1-2/min per card. affected cards spread across rack3, rack7, rack12. no temperature deltas.

sam: any kernel oops or slab traces?

alex: nothing obvious besides repeated EDAC CE messages. pasted quick tail from dmesg:
```
$ sudo dmesg | grep -i edac -n | tail -n 5
[ 82713.123456] EDAC MC0: CE Uncorrected error at node 0, card 1
[ 82718.654321] EDAC MC0: CE Corrected error at node 0, card 4
[ 82724.987654] EDAC MC0: CE Corrected error at node 0, card 1
```

meera: can you paste nvidia-smi ECC counters?

alex: short snapshot:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 1: Volatile ECC: 12
GPU 4: Volatile ECC: 9
GPU 8: Volatile ECC: 11
```

kyle: are these the same SKU we flagged last month (A100-40GB genX)?

lin: I ran the lightweight probe loop on two hosts in rack3 — observed occasional library-level decode retries, ~1 in 5k ops. retries spiked coincident with CE increments.

ops-bot: autoscaler paused on pool gpu-cpu-backfill due to manual override by @sam

sam: thanks bot. my read: non-XID CE drift points at memory/DRAM on the card or VRAM degradation rather than NV driver faults. plan: cohort these GPUs as "suspect" -> graceful drains -> vendor debug -> potential RMA. Also recommend avoiding heavy repro runs on them.

meera: agreed. I've labelled cohort "suspect-ecc-2067" and added GPUs: rack3-g1,g4; rack7-g1; rack12-g2. I'll start graceful drains on non-critical jobs. ETA ~20m.

kyle: short-term mitigation: move latency-sensitive traffic off those hosts to healthy pools and reduce batch sizes on remaining capacity. that should lower stress.

lin: adding telemetry: PSU rails and fans are nominal; no thermal excursions. power cycling a GPU returns no immediate improvement.

alex: logs uploaded -> s3://redwood-ops/2067004321/ (eng-infra/rw). contains dmesg, nvidia-smi samples, probe traces.

sam: vendor ticket opened: VS-8721. asked them for hardware trace capture and suggested memtest on card. if vendor confirms persistent VRAM CE pattern we ask RMA. assigned to @kyle.

ops-bot: notice: rolling drains will consume ~25% spare capacity in region — estimated incremental cost +$1.8/hr while replacements are scheduled.

meera: noted. will inform capacity-sigs but prioritize safety.

kyle: rule of thumb: if any GPU hits CE > 5/min we'll flag it critical and expedite replacement.

lin: scheduling memtest86 variant overnight with readonly pass on affected hosts; will report results morning.

alex: thanks — keeping an eye. will post updates here. :wave:
